If you play the chip, you gain from all four subs; if you do not, you gain from only the best, which is Mykolenko himself.

The record shows three net points gained over eleven decided moves. The model has misfired more often than it has beaten the alternative, so treat its edge as small.

Your team projects 69.0 with Haaland as captain. Salah carries a knock but is 75% likely to play; if he doesn't, Mykolenko comes in, which costs you substantially since he is doubtful himself and projects only 3.1. The captain call is tight — Haaland is 0.3 clear of Salah — but Haaland's ceiling is higher: 25% chance of 10+, versus Salah's uncertainty.

The suggested transfer swaps Wood for Watkins, netting 5.1 points after a 4-point hit. Watkins projects 9.1 ahead over the horizon, making the hit worthwhile on paper, though it depends on that advantage materializing. You have no free transfer, so this is your only lever.

Bench Boost is live this week and worth 14.2 — notably ahead of next week's opportunity by 3.6 points. Playing it now gives you access to Mykolenko's 3.1 and the keeper depth behind Raya, which tilts the scale if Salah's injury risk unsettles you. Without the chip, a benched Mykolenko leaves you exposed.

Three of your outfield are Arsenal, and two each from Liverpool and Manchester City. If you take the Wood-to-Watkins move, the spread tightens slightly but concentration remains high. The model has trended negative so far, so this week's decisions carry weight.
